newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank holds interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank holds interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday that its council had left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.
The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at 3.00 percent.
Markets had little reason to expect any rate action after the central bank said earlier on Thursday its main monetary policy indicator, M3 money supply, grew strongly in January.

Economists said the M3 data, which grew at an annualised rate of 11.7 percent in January compared with the average level in the 1996 fourth quarter, had further dampened any remaining hopes of a further interest rate cut.

A poll of 10 analysts by Reuters this week also showed unanimous opinion in expecting no change in rates, in part due to the stronger dollar acting as a barrier because a further policy move now could appear to sanction a weak mark.
The dollar has risen as high as 1.70 marks since the start of 1997, in defiance of Bundesbank comments which made clear it would be happier with the dollar at around 1.65 marks.
Economists said the dollar's rise, which gives a boost to the German economy by making exports cheaper, had removed some pressure on the Bundesbank to lower rates to help boost growth.
